examples.title: Project header (tempo and meter changes)
examples.fragment:
@project "Name"
  tempo: 120
  time_signature: 4/4
  key: C major
  swing: 56%
  tempo_map: 9:1 = 90
  time_sig_map: 17:1 = 3/4
examples.note: `tempo_map`/`time_sig_map` change tempo and meter at a written bar; the header values are the start. `swing:` is a percentage: the off-beat 8th lands that far late, and a pattern may override it.

examples.title: Named patterns (reusable content)
examples.note: A pattern holds `events:` or `hits:` only; effects, mix and automation belong to the track that hosts the clip.

examples.title: Track with effects, mix and a clip
examples.fragment:
@track bass | preset: punchy_bass, instrument: bass/electric_bass
  effects:
    - compression: ratio=4:1
  mix: vol=-3dB, pan=0, send(reverb=30%), send(delay=15%)
  clip: bass_line [9:1 - 16:4]
examples.note: `send(...)` is a mix property, not a line of its own. Built-in effects: eq, passive_eq, compressor, leveler, opto, fet, iron, doubler, exciter, ducked_send, reverb, delay, chorus, limiter, distortion, flanger, phaser, gate, saturator, stereo_width.

examples.title: Inline phrases (notes directly in tracks)
examples.fragment:
@track piano | instrument: piano/acoustic_grand
  mix: vol=-4dB, pan=0
  @phrase intro [1:1:0 - 8:4:0]
    C4  q   mf
    E4  q   mf  articulation=legato
    G4  h   f
    rest q

examples.title: Several notes at once (one position, comma list)
examples.note: Each member keeps its own duration, dynamics and modifiers; the line advances once, by its longest member. `@N` is an absolute beat position inside the phrase; without it the line follows the previous one.

examples.title: Glissando (slide and run)
examples.note: `gliss` slides from the note's own pitch to the next note's pitch; `gliss=G4` names the destination and `gliss=120ms` arrives that early. A slide needs a builtin preset (`source: builtin, plugin: "builtin.open_synth"`): a sampled preset (SoundFont, sample bank) is a recording and cannot slide, so write `gliss=run` (chromatic) or `gliss=run_diatonic` (the project key) — short notes, which play on any source.

examples.title: Drum notation
examples.note: A hit is `<pad> <beat>:<subdivision>` in the pattern's own bar (16ths 0-3); `xN` repeats that bar. Drums: kick, snare, hat_closed, hat_open, crash, ride, tom_low, clap, rim.

examples.title: Drum kits (@kit)
examples.note: A pad with no playable `layer` falls back to its synthesised `voice`.

examples.title: Placed audio (@audio_clip)
examples.note: The file is relative to the project; parsing and validation do not open it.

examples.title: Automation lanes
examples.note: A bare target (`brightness`) is a control lane: a step list. `<effect>.<param>` (`eq.high_gain`, `fx2.Mix`) is an effect parameter and also takes `curve=`, `tension=`, `smoothing=`, `mode=lfo` with `speed`/`mult`.

examples.title: Buses (shared routing)
examples.fragment:
@bus reverb
  routes: [piano, strings]
  effects:
    - reverb: type=hall, decay=2.5s, mix=100%

examples.title: Master
examples.note: `gain_automation:` is a post-insert ramp on a bus or the master: `linear` or `step`, the range, then points. Points are linear factors (0..1), not dB; the range end is exclusive.

examples.title: Sections and repeat
examples.note: Sections define the rendered timeline; `repeat: N` plays the span N times, so the end can be later than the written one. Edit with `sections_list`, `sections_add`, `sections_set` and `sections_remove`.

examples.title: Sustain pedal
examples.note: `pedal down` holds every note whose note-off happens while it is down; `pedal up` releases them through their normal release. A pedal always carries `@<beat>` and is a phrase or pattern-`events:` line, never a note modifier and never in `hits:`.

examples.title: Crescendo and diminuendo (hairpins)
examples.note: `cresc` / `dim` at `@<beat>` swell from the dynamic in force there to the next written dynamic, or to the phrase end (default pp to f, and f to pp for `dim`); the notes between them take the start level and the ramp runs continuously through them. It expands to a `gain_automation:` clip on the track, which `ocp fmt` shows as a comment under the mark; a sampled instrument's timbre does not brighten with the ramp.
